## Compare height-adjustable desks against your workplace brief

For a Newcastle or Hunter workplace, the decision between fixed-height and sit-stand desks starts with the people, tasks and equipment involved. A product label or a general price multiple does not establish whether a desk suits your team or what the installed package will cost.

Start with a measured brief, assess suitable options and compare written quotes on the same basis. This guide covers the questions to ask before ordering; it does not prescribe an individual workstation setup or promise health, productivity or recruitment outcomes.

[Read the Newcastle office furniture buying guide](/blog/office-furniture-newcastle) for the wider planning process.

## Identify the users and tasks first

Record who will use each position, whether it is shared, the equipment required and any individual needs that should inform selection. Involve the people using the workstations rather than assuming one desk specification suits everyone.

A desk assessment should consider the chair, screens, keyboard, mouse, accessories and the way the work is organised together. [Comcare's computers and workstations guidance](https://www.comcare.gov.au/office-safety-tool/spaces/work-areas/computers-workstations) discusses equipment adjustability, tasks, different users and instruction in setup. Ask a suitable ergonomic or WHS adviser about individual needs or concerns.

Helpful tip: separate a need for equipment adjustment from a need to change the task, layout or work routine. Furniture is one part of the workplace brief.

## Support movement as well as furniture adjustment

[Safe Work Australia's sitting and standing guidance](https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/safety-topic/hazards/sitting-and-standing) discusses managing risks and designing workstations so people can vary posture and movement. It addresses both sitting and standing, rather than treating standing all day as the goal.

[SafeWork NSW's sedentary-work guidance](https://www.safework.nsw.gov.au/safety-starts-here/physical-safety-at-work-the-basics/sedentary-work) includes reviewing tasks, regular movement and changes of posture, with sit-stand desks among the measures to consider. Read the current guidance alongside advice for your workplace and its users. Buying an adjustable desk alone does not establish workplace compliance or an appropriate routine for an individual.

Helpful tip: plan how users will learn the controls and raise concerns after installation. Ask your adviser what setup, instruction and review are appropriate, instead of copying a universal standing schedule.

## Check the specification, not just the motor count

Ask suppliers to identify the exact desk model, top and frame configuration proposed. Compare documented performance against the equipment and users in your brief rather than assuming a particular motor count guarantees stability or suitability.

| Item to compare | Information to request | Practical check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adjustment range | Minimum and maximum heights for the complete desk | Does the proposed configuration suit the intended users and tasks? |
| Working surface | Top size, shape, finish and mounting details | Is there space for the required equipment and working activities? |
| Load and operation | Manufacturer's load rating and operating instructions | Are the planned screens, arms and accessories accounted for? |
| Stability | Relevant product information and assessment or trial options | How does the proposed setup perform at the intended working heights? |
| Controls | Adjustment method, memory functions and instructions | Can users operate the controls clearly and comfortably? |
| Cable management | Proposed routing, available length and accessory compatibility | Can the equipment move through the intended range without snagging? |
| Obstructions | Clearances around storage, screens and neighbouring furniture | What needs relocating or resolving before use? |
| Warranty and service | Written terms, exclusions and claim arrangements | What applies to the frame, controls and other supplied components? |

If a product includes an anti-collision feature, ask how it works and what its limits are. Do not treat it as a replacement for checking the layout and following the manufacturer's instructions.

Helpful tip: record the product codes and supplied documents with the quote. A change of top, frame or accessory can change the package being assessed.

## Resolve shared desks and clusters on the actual plan

For shared positions, consider the range of users and how settings will be adjusted between them. For back-to-back or clustered desks, check the proposed screens, cable routes, under-desk storage and access to each position together.

Test the footprint with chairs and storage in use, not only with everything pushed in. Discuss access, circulation and other site requirements with the relevant designer or adviser. Do not select a fixed-to-adjustable desk ratio solely because another office used it.

Helpful tip: identify retained equipment that may constrain a new desk, such as monitor arms, cable trays or pedestals. Confirm compatibility before assuming it can be transferred.

## Compare current installed quotes

Ask for a fixed-height and an adjustable alternative against the same brief where both are suitable options. Keep quantities, dimensions, finishes, accessories and included services consistent so differences are visible.

Include product supply, GST treatment, freight, assembly, positioning, packaging removal and any agreed work to relocate existing furniture or equipment. List exclusions and any separate specialist work required. Confirm the scope and cost of that work with the appropriate provider.

A weekly figure spread over an assumed lease term is not evidence of savings or return on investment. Make the purchasing decision using the actual quote, budget, intended use and identified requirements.

[Compare installed furniture quotes](/blog/compare-office-furniture-quotes-installed-cost) and [plan the furniture budget](/blog/office-furniture-budget-newcastle).

## Confirm availability and site readiness before ordering

Get written availability information for the exact quantity, model and finish. Distinguish allocated stock, goods to be ordered or made, estimated dispatch, site delivery and installation. A general Newcastle lead-time range cannot confirm when a particular order will be ready.

For the individual building, confirm loading arrangements, lift or stair access, booking rules, work hours and any required induction or documentation. Agree who can approve substitutions and how changes affect price, timing and suitability.

[Use the furniture installation checklist](/blog/office-furniture-installation-checklist-newcastle) to prepare the delivery brief.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much more does a height-adjustable desk cost?

Obtain current comparable quotes for the models and services your workplace needs. The difference depends on the complete specification, quantity, accessories and installed scope. A general per-desk number does not establish your project cost.

### Should every workstation be height-adjustable?

Assess the users, tasks, equipment and relevant advice for each type of setting. Shared and assigned desks can have different requirements. Avoid a universal headcount rule or desk ratio in place of a workplace brief.

### Will sit-stand desks improve attendance or productivity?

This guide does not promise those outcomes. Ask staff about their work needs and review how the space supports them. Consider furniture alongside the wider work environment and how tasks are organised.

### How should we check workstation suitability?

Use current official guidance, manufacturer information and appropriate workplace-specific advice. Include setup instruction and a way for users to report concerns. Product selection alone does not determine the workplace's legal position or an individual's needs.

### How long will delivery take in Newcastle?

Ask the supplier to confirm the actual products, quantities and finishes, then the delivery and installation arrangements for your building. Keep estimates and dependencies visible and reconfirm them before committing the move-in programme.
